data.body:
OPERATOR-RATIFIED DECISION (2026-08-04) — recorded before implementation, per instruction.

rebar must handle local git lock contention AUTOMATICALLY, with NO escalation to the agent
running the command. Concretely:

- A PER-STORE ADVISORY LOCK plus BOUNDED JITTERED RETRY/BACKOFF on the store's git call
  sites, consistent with the existing push-retry pattern in rebar._store.push.
- Transient lock conflicts (index.lock / ref locks briefly held by a peer) resolve SILENTLY —
  at most a debug/warning log.
- Only a genuinely stuck lock (bounded timeout exhausted) surfaces an actionable error naming
  the lock file and holder guidance.
- Bounded defaults on the order of tens of seconds total wait, jittered. Config-tunable ONLY
  if a store/git config surface already exists — it does not (checked docs/config.md
  inventory + src/rebar/config.py), so NO new config keys (inert/one-off config is a known
  defect class here).

Operator context: "We've seen a lot of contention with parallel sessions" — the commissioning
session itself observed a claim fail on a store lock and succeed on manual retry. (Also
reproduced while working this ticket: `run_ensures: write lock unavailable, skipping sweep:
flock: could not acquire lock after 60s` on a plain read command.)

This decision selects among the options the OSS research (comments above) left open: bounded
jittered retry (git lockfile.c's jittered backoff shape, Mercurial's bounded wait) + own-lock
serialization (JGit's in-process fair lock before the file lock; git-annex's single-flusher
rule), rather than block-forever (cargo/Bazel) or fail-fast. Research recs #1 (age ceiling)
landed separately as 5389; rec #4 (jitter on the store-lock sleeps) is folded into this
ticket's implementation.

STRICT TDD is an operator condition for this bug class: RED behavioral tests first —
(a) a git op hitting a transient index.lock held briefly by another process succeeds after
retry with no error surfaced; (b) a permanently held lock produces one actionable error after
the bounded timeout; (c) uncontended ops have no added latency (no sleep on the happy path).
